# Reference-aware relation-binding acceptance (#52)

Revision `fce80ed7500252227d6a50f6d3fabdd442c7c22c` is the measured
relation-binding candidate. The renderer is the only backend path that emits
`materialize()`: every binding declares its expression, consumer count,
completed safe reductions, stable-evaluation requirement, and measured-cache
exception. The complete decision audit is in
[`RELATION-BINDING.md`](../../RELATION-BINDING.md).

## Correctness

The frozen acceptance manifest SHA-256 is
`38701686e0a423b30776c5ea1d145fdfe3774100842c24cf5743c81c2f90184e`.
All **255/255** strict fixtures passed against Kusto
`2026.11.15.0741-2645-8e3387b-master`: HTTP 200, exactly one empty multiset or
schema diagnostic, one successful uncancelled completion, and no error frame.
The fixtures cover multiplicity, exact windows, context relationships, stable
shared IDs, chaining, reporting bounds/lookback, aliases, mappings, and public
diagnostics.

The broad benchmark manifest SHA-256 is
`89f564281cb100681c5dde848414470bcce07aebecd829cb73884754ade4aa09`.
All **384/384** final samples passed exact independent results and declared
schemas: six repetitions of all 64 established workloads. The focused manifest
SHA-256 is
`acbe462e507efce5387762cbf01b3d938ddef2349d9958f9d6cc45a3d31a2fd4`;
all **42/42** focused samples passed across sparse/dense/hot density, unique and
repeated values, one/two display consumers, Boolean context, ordered context,
and context-bearing child reuse.

Every run used the same immutable engine image
`sha256:65e8298d9350856dec696e0e41327288e7bc105146768a1429fce62f3640acd8`,
12,884,901,888-byte container/query memory and swap, no CPU quota, disabled
query-result cache, and 15-second client / 13-second server limits.

## Adoption and negative evidence

The 64 final queries contain 102 `materialize()` calls versus 166 in the #51
baseline, and total 174,559 generated bytes versus 175,415. Twenty-eight query
hashes changed. Ordinary single-use context matching, Boolean participant
selection, final ordered participant filtering, and one-field display-only
relationship stages no longer consume cache unless measurements justify an
exception. Shared child results, stable correlation IDs, reused exact
percentile candidates, value-count source/activity relations, and genuinely
reused ordered witnesses remain cached after their safe reductions.

An initial six-sample broad run passed **384/384** and measured median
per-workload ratios of 0.991 CPU, 1.000 peak memory, 1.010 client elapsed, and
1.001 engine elapsed against #51. The exact final hot-group value-sum context
query reduced median CPU by 46% and client elapsed by 17%, satisfying the 15%
target threshold. Several millisecond-scale historical ratios crossed the 10%
noise guard, so the four suspect workloads were rerun for 12 samples and the
exact frozen #51 queries were rerun contemporaneously.

Those paired runs selected these measured exceptions:

- value-count keeps `WindowSourceMatches` but not the one-consumer complete
  relationship cache: median CPU was 38% lower and peak memory 23.5% lower than
  the contemporaneous #51 query;
- percentile keeps `WindowSourceMatches` but not the one-consumer complete
  relationship cache: median CPU was 32% lower with equal median peak memory;
  removing the window cache produced a repeatable bimodal plan and a 77% median
  peak-memory increase in the broad run;
- value-average retains both caches: the removal candidate missed the 15%
  adoption threshold, while the retained pair measured 19.6% lower median CPU
  than the contemporaneous #51 query.

The rejected removal, window-only, and fully retained prototypes all completed
successfully. Their exact manifests, queries, request/response frames, and
12-sample result ledgers are preserved in `benchmark-raw-evidence.tar.gz` and
the named JSON ledgers. Unchanged plain-query controls also shifted by more than
10% elapsed between broad runs, so those historical elapsed ratios are treated
as run-level timing drift rather than candidate regressions; the paired
same-engine reruns decide the cache exceptions.

## Files

- `acceptance-manifest.json`, `acceptance-results.json`, and
  `acceptance-raw-evidence.tar.gz` freeze the complete strict engine gate.
- `benchmark-manifest.json` and `benchmark-results.json` freeze the final
  64-workload gate.
- `focused-manifest.json` and `focused-results.json` freeze the seven focused
  relation-binding workloads.
- `initial-removal-results.json`, `removal-rerun-results.json`,
  `window-cache-results.json`, `full-cache-results.json`, and
  `source-shaping-contemporary-results.json` preserve adoption and negative
  evidence.
- `benchmark-raw-evidence.tar.gz` contains every frozen candidate query/fixture
  and the raw final/prototype/baseline request and response files.
- `SHA256SUMS` authenticates every published artifact.

These synthetic results establish correctness and the stated relative behavior
for the recorded hashes and resource settings. They are not a production
throughput or capacity SLA.
